## Objective

To build a transcriptome-wide, placental miRNA-–mRNA regulatory network using CANDLE data.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)  ## tidy data framework, ggplot2, pipes
library(assertthat) ## sanity checks
library(here)       ## sets path nicely for markdown
library(broom)      ## for tidy correlation test results
library(parallel)   ## to paralellize the Spearman correlations
```
 

```{r}
## read data
## miRNA expression: loads miRNA, CPM, covar
load(file = here::here("network_construction/intermediateData/clean_miRNA.Rdata"))
## mRNA expression
load(file = here::here("network_construction/intermediateData/clean_RNAseq.Rdata"))
## mRNA targets of miRNA
load(file = here::here("network_construction/intermediateData/predicted_targets_complete.RData"))

## read annotation files
## use the annotation file from the mRNA seq alignment
## use the annotation file from the mRNA seq alignment
annot <- read_csv(here::here("network_construction/intermediateData/annotation_proteincoding_refseq.csv"))
```

## Network Analysis

First, we will identify the list of predicted targets (see `02_clean_targetscan_mirdb.Rmd`). 
Then, we will write a function to do cor_test on each set of putative pairs. 

```{r}
edgelist <- simplified_targets |>
  ## limit to only the miRNA and mRNA we have data on
  dplyr::filter(ensembl_gene_id %in% annot_mRNA$ENSEMBL) |>
  dplyr::filter(miRNA %in% annot_mir$name) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

## unique sets of pairs
unique_pairs <- edgelist$miRNA_mRNA_pair |> unique()

## now, make a single data set with all miRNA and mRNA
joint_data <- dplyr::full_join(
  ## start with miRNA
  CPM_mir |>
    t() |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "pathways_id"), 
  ## now, mRNA. Note names will be ENSEMBL ids, need to fix after correlations next
  CPM_mRNA |>
    t() |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "pathways_id"),
  by = join_by(pathways_id)
)

rm(RNASeq, miRNA, CPM_mir, CPM_mRNA, simplified_targets, union_of_targets)
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include=TRUE}
weights <- mclapply(unique_pairs, function(x) {
  ## get names as character strings
  miRNA_name <- unlist(strsplit(x, " "))[1]
  mRNA_name <- unlist(strsplit(x, " "))[2]
  
  temp <- with(joint_data, cor.test(get(miRNA_name), get(mRNA_name),
                                    method = "spearman", 
                                    exact = FALSE)) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    dplyr::mutate(miRNA = miRNA_name, mRNA_target = mRNA_name)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
```

This takes a long time to run locally (approximately an hour and a half), so we will write `weights` to a file. 

```{r eval=FALSE, include=TRUE}
write_csv(weights, here::here("network_construction", "weights_allPredictedPairs.csv"))
```

Now, only retain negative, two-tailed Spearman correlations that meet FDR<0.05.

```{r}
weights <- read_csv(here::here("network_construction", "weights_allPredictedPairs.csv"))

edges <- weights |>
  dplyr::mutate(miRNA_mRNA_pair = paste(miRNA, mRNA_target, sep = " ")) |>
  dplyr::select(miRNA, mRNA_target, miRNA_mRNA_pair, cor = estimate, p.value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(FDR = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) |>
  dplyr::filter(cor < 0) |>
  dplyr::filter(FDR < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
```

Write the edge list and nodes to CSV for Cytoscape or further analysis in `R` using igraph. 

```{r}
nodes <- dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(node = annot_mir$name, 
                                         type = "miRNA"),
                          tibble::tibble(node = annot_mRNA$ENSEMBL, 
                                         type = "target")
                          ) |>
  dplyr::filter(node %in% c(unique(edges$miRNA), unique(edges$mRNA_target)))

write_csv(nodes, here::here("network_construction", "allPairs_nodes_20240719.csv"))
write_csv(edges, here::here("network_construction", "allPairs_edges_20240719.csv"))
```
